Reporting to the Head of New Business, this role combines new partner acquisition with early-stage partner development, ensuring new relationships scale rapidly, deliver value, and contribute to Gamma's long-term growth ambitions. This role is suited to a commercially driven sales professional who thrives in complex partner environments, enjoys opening new strategic relationships, and can balance consultative selling with hands-on commercial execution. What will you be doing day-to-day? New Partner Acquisition Identify, target, and acquire new service provider partners aligned to Gamma's Service Provider growth strategy. Develop a deep understanding of the UK service provider, telecoms, cloud communications, and carrier landscape. Lead end-to-end partner acquisition activity, from market mapping and prospecting through to commercial negotiation and contract signature. Build and maintain strong executive-level relationships with prospective partners, positioning Gamma as a strategic long-term supplier. Create and execute account plans for target prospects, ensuring a structured approach to partner acquisition. High-Potential Partner Growth Own and grow a portfolio of newly onboarded, high-potential service provider partners, driving rapid revenue growth and partner activation. Work closely with internal stakeholders to ensure partners are successfully onboarded, enabled, and supported. Manage senior stakeholder relationships across both customer and internal Gamma teams. Provide market insight, customer feedback, and competitive intelligence to support Gamma's wider Service Provider strategy. Support partner onboarding and transition into longer-term account management or strategic account teams where appropriate. Contribute to the continuous improvement of sales processes, partner engagement models, and go-to-market initiatives. Pipeline Management & Governance Own and manage a healthy new business pipeline, maintaining strong forecasting discipline through Gamma's CRM systems. Pipeline health, forecasting accuracy, and sales governance compliance. Contribution to overall Service Provider Business Unit growth objectives. What You’ll Bring Essential: Significant experience within telecoms, UCaaS, CCaaS, cloud communications, connectivity, mobile, or wholesale communications markets. Proven track record of new business acquisition and partner development. Experience managing and closing complex, high-value B2B sales opportunities. Strong commercial acumen with the ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders and executive decision-makers. Excellent negotiation, presentation, and relationship management skills. Self-motivated and capable of operating effectively in a home-based environment. Strong pipeline management and forecasting discipline. Desirable: Existing network within the UK service provider, carrier, telecoms, cloud, or channel ecosystem. Experience working with service providers, wholesale operators, MSPs, UCaaS providers, and CCaaS providers. Knowledge of Gamma's portfolio, channel model, or wholesale telecommunications markets. Experience using HubSpot or equivalent CRM platforms. Understanding of SIP, voice, mobile, cloud communications, or communications enablement technologies. What do we offer you? 25 days annual leave + birthday Subsidised private medical insurance 5.1% matched pension contributions Enhanced parental leave Life assurance and Income protection Share save and incentive plans Electric Vehicle and Cycle scheme Employee discounts Volunteer day A few things to note We require all candidates to be eligible to work in the UK and pass a basic DBS check. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, especially those underrepresented in our industry. As a family-friendly employer, we foster a culture of trust, autonomy, and flexibility to support your work-life balance and help you thrive at Gamma. For recruitment agencies – we have a network of fantastic partners that support us in our hiring from time to time. We’re not looking to increase that network currently, so please don’t send speculative CVs.

review_candidates.title: Site Contracts & Budget Manager (Romania)
review_candidates.description: The Site Contracts & Budget Manager provides operational leadership for site contracting and budget negotiation activities across awarded clinical trials. The role is primarily accountable for contracting strategy, Clinical Trial Agreement negotiation and execution, site budget negotiations, amendments, and resolution of complex contractual and financial issues. Working in close partnership with the Site Budget & Proposal Manager, the role translates proposal-stage budget assumptions into effective study- and site-level contracting and negotiation strategies. Together, the roles provide complementary leadership across the site budget and contracting lifecycle, with distinct primary areas of accountability. The Site Contracts & Budget Manager serves as a key contact and escalation point for sponsors, sites, and internal stakeholders and provides functional guidance, training, and support to Site Budget & Contracting personnel Requirements: More specifically, the Site Contracts and Budget Manager must: Lead and manage Site Budget & Contracting staff, providing direction, coaching, development, workload oversight, and support to ensure consistent quality and delivery across assigned studies. Oversee site contracting and budget negotiation activities across the portfolio, ensuring appropriate resourcing, prioritization, quality, timelines, and escalation of risks or issues. Provide oversight of site contracting for awarded clinical trials, including Clinical Trial Agreements, associated financial exhibits, amendments, negotiation parameters, and country-specific requirements. Establish and maintain contracting strategies, standards, and negotiation approaches that support timely site activation while balancing sponsor requirements, organizational standards, site expectations, and contractual risk. Serve as functional escalation point for complex or high-risk contract and budget negotiations, providing guidance to team members and facilitating decisions with sponsors, sites, Legal Affairs, and other stakeholders. Oversee the operational implementation of study-specific site budgets, including negotiation parameters, approval pathways, exceptions, and escalation requirements. Translate proposal-stage budget assumptions into executable study- and site-level budget and contracting strategies. Collaborate with Legal Affairs, Project Management, Study Start-Up, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Operations, Finance, and other stakeholders to ensure contracting and budget activities align with study requirements and operational plans. Provide site contracting expertise during proposal development, including input on country-specific contracting requirements, anticipated timelines, institutional considerations, negotiation trends, risks, and resource needs. Participate and/or support bid defence meetings, client presentations, and sponsor strategy discussions when site contracting, budget negotiation, timelines, or associated risks are relevant. Monitor portfolio-level contracting and budget performance, identifying emerging risks, delays, capacity constraints, quality concerns, and opportunities for improvement. Own and oversee the business assets supporting Site Budget & Contracting, including contract and budget templates, negotiation tools, country intelligence, guidance documents, trackers, reference materials, and other functional resources. Ensure business assets remain current, fit for purpose, consistently applied, appropriately governed, and aligned with evolving operational and business needs. Oversee the integrity, consistency, and usability of Site Budget & Contracting data across applicable tools, trackers, and systems. Use contracting and negotiation outcomes to strengthen institutional and country intelligence and, in partnership with the Site Budget & Proposal Manager, inform future budget assumptions and benchmarks. Lead functional process improvement initiatives to improve contracting and budget negotiation quality, efficiency, consistency, scalability, and stakeholder experience. Support digital transformation and automation opportunities that reduce manual activities, strengthen controls, and improve the availability and quality of contracting and budget data. Establish and monitor relevant performance indicators and use operational data to identify trends, bottlenecks, and opportunities for corrective action or continuous improvement. Ensure Site Budget & Contracting staff are appropriately trained and consistently apply relevant SOPs, processes, templates, tools, and quality standards. Partner with senior leadership on resource and capacity planning, functional priorities, process maturity, systems and tools, quality, and continuous improvement. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, proactive risk management, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement within the Site Budget & Contracting team. Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training. PROFILE B.Sc. or in a relevant field of study. 5+ years of experience in clinical research, clinical trial budgeting, or related financial management roles within the pharmaceutical, biotech, or CRO industry. Strong negotiation and communication skills to engage with sponsors, external budget contacts, and internal stakeholders, serving as the escalation point to secure optimal study budgets. Experience creating and maintaining budget templates tailored to global regions and therapeutic areas, ensuring scalability and consistency. Collaborative mindset to partner with operational leads and ensure financial assumptions align with study design, operational strategies, and delivery plans. Experience representing the organization in bid defense meetings and client calls, with the confidence to explain budget rationale and defend assumptions. Technical proficiency to maintain pricing tools, cost databases, and budget models in collaboration with Finance and IT teams. Leadership abilities to train and mentor junior specialists, provide guidance, and ensure team adherence to best practices. Demonstrated success in partnering with senior team members to refine internal processes, drive efficiencies, and improve deliverables. Strategic thinking to engage with leadership on process improvement initiatives, offering insights and recommendations that enhance operational excellence. Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines. Our company: Romania: The work environment At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability, and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities. In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks: Permanent full-time position Flexible schedule Vacation Home-based position Ongoing learning and development About Indero Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint. Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale. Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request. Indero only accepts applicants who can legally work in Romania.
